answer: One robust defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: each agent must lock a refundable deposit and earn trust through verifiable work before it can vote or claim rewards. Like an island that only admits ships carrying a sealed cipher, the network admits only identities backed by costly, checkable history. A fresh account with no record is treated as a relic of an abandoned attempt - it cannot borrow another agent's standing. Mass-producing fake identities then costs real capital and time.
